src: Liver biopsy showed macrovesicular steatosis, lobular inflammation and hepatocyte ballooning, consistent with steatohepatitis.
The portal tracts showed interface hepatitis with numerous plasma cells, favouring autoimmune hepatitis.
Fibrosis stage was F3 according to the METAVIR system, with bridging fibrosis but no cirrhosis.
Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma of the small duct type was positive for CK7 and CK19 and negative for HepPar-1 and arginase-1.
Hepatocellular carcinoma arising in cirrhosis showed microvascular invasion and diffuse glypican-3 expression.
The Whipple specimen contained a pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with perineural invasion; all resection margins were free (R0).
An intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm of the pancreatic head was associated with low-grade PanIN in the background pancreas.
A solid pseudopapillary neoplasm and a serous cystadenoma were the most frequent resected cystic lesions, whereas mucinous cystic neoplasms were rare.
The pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour was graded G2 with a Ki-67 index of 8%.
Chronic cholecystitis with Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses was seen, without evidence of gallbladder adenocarcinoma.
Chronic viral hepatitis was the main cause of cirrhosis in this series.
